text.p: Hewlett-Packard Co and Fluke Corp have formed a worldwide marketing and distribution alliance covering certain electronic testing products, the two companies said Wednesday.

Under the agreement selected Fluke distributors will sell products from Hewlett-Packard's basic instruments line, while Hewlett-Packard will sell and support several of Fluke's compact electronic test tools.
No money changed hands in the agreement, officials said.
Bill Parzybok, chairman and chief executive officer of Fluke, said in an interview that the deal was important but initially would result in only "a few million dollars" in annual sales for Fluke.
Officials said the Fluke oscilloscopes, multimeters, logic probes and other devices covered by the agreement are complementary with Hewlett-Packard's scopes and meters.
But the two companies will continue to "compete vigorously" in other product areas, Hewlett-Packard vice president Larry Potter said.
Parzybok said the deal could not have happened in the past, before Fluke moved to more specific handheld devices that do not compete directly with Hewlett-Packard products.
